beats.text: MRP-VM presents an architecture for building and improving custom agent systems under explicit control.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Its central distinction is between a successful answer and a maintained organizational capability.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The book explains how procedures, evidence, permissions, and versions can stay connected.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: A proposed improvement must remain separate from the authority that activates it.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Readers can examine that design without mistaking its research ambitions for proven reliability.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: A successful response may depend on assumptions that nobody recorded for the next request.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The book proposes maintaining procedures, tests, and interpreters as versioned Agentic Knowledge Units.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Explicit plans connect work with dependencies and qualifications for its results.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: This creates a place to preserve how a recurring task should be performed.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The research question is whether that structure produces more repeatable, governable capability.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Operational feedback can motivate a candidate revision without changing the active procedure immediately.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The proposed process compares candidates against baselines and checks for regressions.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Proposal, evaluation, approval, and activation remain separate responsibilities.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Published versions retain a coherent identity and a target for rollback.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The book uses these distinctions to connect improvement with control over consequential change.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Start with the gap between a good answer and a repeatable organizational practice.
